**Allowed origins** are set by the `origin` callback passed to `cors({...})` in `worker/src/index.ts:19-35`. It echoes the request origin back if one of these is true:
- The origin is exactly `http://localhost:4200`.
- The origin ends with `.pages.dev`, at any subdomain depth.
- The origin ends with `.workers.dev`, at any subdomain depth.

Requests with no `Origin` header, and any other origin, get `null`, so no CORS headers are sent.

The same `cors()` call also sets:
- `allowMethods`: GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS
- `allowHeaders`: Content-Type, Authorization
- `maxAge`: 86400

**Adding a custom domain:** edit the `if` condition at `worker/src/index.ts:23-27`. Add another clause such as `|| origin === 'https://play.example.com'`. For wildcard subdomains, add an `origin.endsWith('.example.com')` clause. Use the full scheme and host for an exact match.

Don't put the domain in an array. Hono matches array entries as exact strings, so wildcards won't work there. That is why the code uses a function. `docs/code/worker/src/index.md` documents this, and it points to DEPLOYMENT_NOTES §4 for more.

Two other things to know:
- The Worker doesn't need a `wrangler.toml` change for CORS. That file only declares the bindings (`AI`, `SESSION_KV`, `DB`, `ENVIRONMENT`).
- The `endsWith` checks match any host with that suffix. `.pages.dev` and `.workers.dev` are shared platforms, so any site on them can call the API. Match custom domains tightly.

I didn't open `docs/DEPLOYMENT_NOTES.md`, so check §4 there for custom-domain steps outside the Worker, such as the Pages domain setup.
